_comment_version_1_90_0: 1.89.0 -> 1.90.0: shared sign-in between the fleet's own apps on one phone (Ray: "its one device and same account so i expect them to use same token"). New SessionHandoff (exported) is the transport: open(package) opens another fleet app carrying a hand-off, takePending() reads the one this app was opened with, addListener() fires when one arrives while running. What is handed over is auth_sdk's (it sets SessionHandoff.payloadProvider); without it every call is a no-op. Android channel rokct.base_sdk/session_handoff (SessionHandoffBridge.kt, registered in MainActivity). Only same-key apps can talk: the hand-off enters only through SessionHandoffActivity, guarded by the signature-level permission rokct.permission.SESSION_HANDOFF that AndroidManifest.xml now defines and uses, and the sender checks the target's signature and addresses it by explicit component. host_integration and platform_permissions carry the activity and uses-permission for shells whose AndroidManifest.xml is not re-extracted; the <permission> definition itself sits outside <application>, which host_integration cannot reach, so such a shell needs the template's <permission> block or the hand-off stays off (the start is refused and the app opens the ordinary way).

_comment_version_1_73_0: 1.72.3 -> 1.73.0: one demo seam in the HTTP layer (Ray, 2026-09-25: "Demo skips the real code"). New DemoGatewayInterceptor, first on every HttpService Dio client, answers POST /api/v1/method/rokct.platform.api from <cmd>.json fixture files while DemoSession.demoActive - read per request, never cached - so a demo session runs the REAL repository and only the network hop is replaced. SDKs register fixture asset directories with DemoFixtures.registerAssetDirectory. A known cmd resolves with its fixture (the value inside Frappe's message envelope); an unknown cmd in demo fails with DemoFixtureMissing naming the cmd, never a silent pass and never the network. Fixtures may use $now_iso / $now_ms tokens and a $demo_select object (by payload.<field> or role). Outside a demo session it is a pass-through; non-gateway paths pass through too, so SDKs still routing demo through their own Demo repositories are unaffected. Demo login and demo data are unchanged.

_comment_version_1_69_0: 1.68.0 -> 1.69.0: the host offers one more optional Kotlin bridge, AppChangesBridge, so a launcher shell can be told when the device's installed apps change (Ray, 2026-09-21: "how do other launchers remember when app has installed and put icon in their screen?"). database._comment: No 'tables' key on purpose. base_sdk's own tables (KeyValueTable, OutboxTable, IdMappingsTable) are declared directly in the @DriftDatabase annotation in lib/src/database/app_database.dart, and the installer COPIES every table source named here into base_sdk's own package to import relatively - so listing them would compile two copies of each class. Only the migration is declared.
database._comment_migration: THE MIGRATION VERSION NUMBER IS SHARED WITH EVERY OTHER SDK IN THE APP, AND IS NOT THIS SDK'S TO COUNT ALONE. sdk_installer_base.py update_database_registration() sets the composed AppDatabase's schemaVersion to the MAXIMUM version any composed manifest declares, while each SDK writes its own `if (from < N)` guard into the one shared onUpgrade - one namespace, no allocator. Drift calls onUpgrade only when schemaVersion is GREATER than the stored user_version, so a number at or below the running maximum runs nothing at all on a device that is already there, and the column this step adds would simply never appear (productivity_sdk lost its notes table to exactly this, and this manifest's number is chosen the way that manifest's comment says to). Two further traps are specific to base: the composer SUBSTITUTES the schemaVersion getter in app_database.dart, so a base-owned number written only in Dart is erased at compose time; and max_version is only raised inside the installer's `if version and step` branch, so a version declared without a step raises nothing. Hence both, declared here. VERSIONS READ ACROSS THE FLEET BEFORE CLAIMING 19 (every manifest.json outside a .rokct/cache in every repo reachable from this workspace, read at their current main): radio_sdk 18 (agent/radio/dart), productivity_sdk 17 (productivity/productivity/dart), auth_sdk 16 (Users/auth/dart), agent_sdk 15 (agent/agent/dart), replay_sdk 15 (agent/replay/dart), subscriptions_sdk 15 (agent/subscriptions/dart), polaris_sdk 13 (corporate/polaris/dart), fav_sdk 12 (agent/fav/dart); no other manifest declares a database.migration at all - base_sdk, launch_sdk, comms_sdk and telemetry_sdk in this repo included, until now. 19 is above all of them. NOTE for whoever reads this next: radio_sdk's 17 and productivity_sdk's 17 are a LIVE COLLISION on that number (radio's own comment still records productivity at 14), which is not this PR's to fix but is the same defect all of this text is about. The step is idempotent - ensureOwnerScopeColumns() checks for the column before touching anything - and beforeOpen in app_database.dart calls it on every open as a floor, so a device that somehow skips this step still gets the column rather than throwing on its first read.

_comment_app_type: The tenant remote-config boot absorbed from the retired host lib/utils/app_initializer.dart files (manager migration M5, driver M4). Flavor-gated because the fetch is per-app ('app_type=Manager' / 'app_type=Driver'); other flavors declare their own entry with their own app_type string when they flip to fully generated shells. base_sdk has no lib/src/manager|driver role folders - declaring the personas only carries these hooks (role-stripping is a no-op for base).
